Resolves #18962

Related: #18762

🪢 *Sort the grid by a column, edit a cell in it: the row stays where it is, and the header goes on saying "ascending". Contract or accident? The guide did not say, and no arm would have noticed a change.*

## What changes

- `learn/guides/datahandling/Grids.md`, "What Scrolling Does to an Edit": a commit moves no row, even into the sorted column; sorters apply when they change, and the next header click puts the row where its value belongs.
- One arm on the public example, driven by header clicks and keys only: sort ascending, commit `Zzz` into the first row with Tab — the next editor opens in the same row and the row keeps its place — then two header clicks sort it to the end.

No source change. The ticket records the decision: the row stays put, because an edit that teleports its row mid Tab-walk is the worse default; re-sorting when an edit ends is a store-wide change and out of scope.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium, header clicks and keys, CI-executed e2e tier) → L3 required (AC-1…AC-3). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the PR baseline jobs run in CI. Change class: zero-delta (`docs`).

Micro-review eligible: docs + one arm — no source line changes.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | The guide passage, `Grids.md` "What Scrolling Does to an Edit". |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `e2e/grid/CellEditingExample.spec.mjs` › `a commit into the sorted column moves no row, and the next sort puts it where it belongs`. |
| AC-3 | "moves no row" + "Tab goes on in the row" → the arm's Tab step and its position read; "the next click on the header" → its last two clicks. The filter half is NOT in the guide: measured on the pooled fixture only, no arm on the public example could drive it. |

## Deltas from ticket

The guide names sorting only; the ticket first said "sorted or filtered". Ticket body amended in place.

## Test Evidence

Mutation — `data.Store#onRecordChange` re-sorts after firing: the arm goes red at `the committed row kept its place`. `--repeat-each=20`: 20 of 20. The arm sits mid-file, so it does not collide with #18953's arms at the spec's end.
